narrative.overview:
Crates N' Plates looks like a diner's order pad and receipt made rigorous. The surface is warm and plainspoken — a neighbourhood diner's voice carried straight into the interface — but it is disciplined by a bookkeeper's columns: money is tabular, labels are small and set in uppercase, and every figure the system can compute it computes, so the screen never asks a person to do arithmetic. The system spans one web app with four very different jobs (a customer ordering on a phone, a cashier at a shared register, a cook glancing at a wall screen, and an owner in the back office), so the visual system stays deliberately quiet and consistent rather than expressive: it earns trust by being legible under service light and identical from screen to screen.

Depth is tonal, not shadowed. The page sits on a near-black chalk surface, cards and panels lift onto a slightly lighter board surface, and a 1px line does the rest of the separating. There is effectively no shadow vocabulary — the one exception is an inset ring marking a late kitchen ticket — so hierarchy comes from surface layering, borders, and spacing, never from drop shadows. The feel is refined and restrained: quiet surfaces, precise alignment, no flourish. Controls are honest and unfussy rather than decorative.

Color is almost entirely neutral; a single warm red accent does all the signalling. It is used wherever it matters — the primary action, the active nav item, a promo tag, and every exception the diner must notice (a late ticket, a refunds-owed badge, a flagged payment hold, a NEW badge). Because it is the only hue in the system (bar one green "open" dot), each appearance reads as emphasis rather than decoration. Typography is the system UI stack: no webfont is loaded, so the app renders instantly and matches each device's native feel. Two motifs carry the brand more than any single color: uppercase, letter-spaced micro-labels (order codes, column headers, step counters) and tabular numerals on every monetary figure, which keep the ledger columns aligned.
keyCharacteristics: Flat tonal layering: chalk base → board raised → 1px border; essentially no shadows.
One warm red accent, used wherever the eye must go next or an exception lives; the only other hue is a green "open" status dot.
Tabular numerals on every money figure; uppercase letter-spaced labels on every micro-label.
System UI font stack, no webfont; dark-first with a full prefers-color-scheme: light mirror.
Pills and soft radii (6 / 12 / 20px) over hard corners; touch targets floored at 44px.
Motion is minimal and only ever transform/opacity, always disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one accent hue in the system (Accent Red) plus one functional green dot. No second brand color is introduced; new emphasis reuses Accent Red rather than adding a hue.

rules.name: The Every-Exception Rule
rules.body: Accent Red is not decoration and not confined to "primary" roles: it marks the primary action and every exception the diner must notice (late, refunds owed, flagged hold, NEW). If a state needs attention, it goes red — it does not get a new color.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every monetary figure — prices, totals, change, receipt lines, KPI values, kitchen quantities — sets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Digits align in columns; a computed number never jitters.

rules.name: The Ledger-Label Rule
rules.body: Any label under ~1rem that names a column, field, or metric is uppercase with 0.04em letter-spacing. Order codes and large identifiers invert this: large, bold, 0.08–0.12em tracking, never uppercase.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and in every state. Never add a drop shadow to imply elevation — raise the surface tone (chalk → board) and let the 1px line hold the edge.

rules.name: The Border-Over-Shadow Rule
rules.body: When something must feel lifted or focused, the answer is a border color change (to Accent Red) or an outline — never a shadow or a glow.

dos: Do keep the surface stack to Chalk → Board and separate with a 1px Line.
Do set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every monetary figure.
Do set micro-labels (columns, fields, metrics) uppercase with 0.04em tracking, and order codes large, bold, and 0.08–0.12em tracked.
Do use Accent Red for both the primary action and every exception (late, refunds owed, flagged hold, NEW); it is the only accent.
Do floor touch targets at 44px on cashier/kitchen surfaces and never below 24px anywhere (WCAG 2.5.8).
Do confine motion to transform/opacity and disable it under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
Do carry the radius scale 6 / 12 / 20px plus pills — no square corners.
donts: Don't add a drop shadow to imply elevation; raise the surface tone instead.
Don't introduce a second brand hue — the only non-red color is the single-purpose green "open" dot (#2f9e44).
Don't use Accent Red as a large background fill for decoration; it is for emphasis and exceptions (the announcement banner is the one sanctioned large fill).
Don't load a webfont or add a mono face — the system stack plus tabular figures is the whole type system.
Don't re-render, recolor, or re-export the logo (public/images/logo.png, white-on-transparent, always on its Board chip) or the GCash QR (always the official white image inside the red frame).
Don't put two same-weight, same-style buttons in one visual group — the hierarchy comes from size, contrast, and grouping.
Don't hide navigation behind an unlabeled icon; chrome stays visible and labeled.
